The generated cases mostly have empty cores — peeling removes everything in round 1. That's because random walks in a small graph produce paths where every link has an endpoint witness. I need to generate cases with nontrivial cores to test inference properly.

Looking at the endpoint-cycle example: 3 paths forming a cycle where each link appears with both endpoints interior in some path. To get a nontrivial core, we need for each surviving link {u,v}: some path where u is interior and some path where v is interior (both containing the link).

Strategy: generate paths that are "long walks" covering the graph such that each edge appears in the middle of some path for both endpoints. E.g., take a cycle graph and generate all rotations of the cycle as paths (like the endpoint-cycle example). Or take a graph and generate random long walks (length 5-8) — with enough walks, each edge will appear in interior positions.

Key insight: a link {u,v} survives round 1 iff there's a path where u is interior (and containing the link) AND a path where v is interior. If walks are long enough and numerous, most edges satisfy this.
